parsed.elsewhere_quote: if $g\ge2$ the product at least halves, if $g=1$ the product is kept but $z$ increases by $1$ (and $z$ never decreases), so there are at most $\lfloor\log_2 P_0\rfloor + 2026$ moves. Moreover no move can produce two $1$'s, so some entry $>1$ always survives, and the terminal position has **exactly one** entry $M>1$.
parsed.explanation: The objection is correct: when $g=1$, $\ell=\operatorname{lcm}(m,n)=mn$, not $m+n$. The same sentence immediately gives the correct output $(1,mn)$, and the write-up elsewhere correctly states and uses the product/number-of-ones argument and proves that an entry greater than 1 survives. Thus L1.1 is established despite the isolated false formula. Deleting the plus sign in $m+n$ repairs it to $mn$.
